top_choice_rationale: P002 has the most direct prediction-to-experiment chain on the slate: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model of magic-angle flat bands is exactly the system in which Jarillo-Herrero's group found correlated insulators and superconductivity, and the phenomena are reproduced widely. With a citation limited to the flat-band prediction and the observed states, and silent on the pairing mechanism, it rewards what is established. Reservations are about seven years of maturity and Cao and the co-first authors falling outside three names. I rank P003 second for its two decades of confirmation and cleanest two-name credit, and P001 third because the HgTe experiment tested the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal rather than Kane-Mele, so its three-name allocation cannot be repaired by wording. A prize is preferable to none.
